sanskrit_verse:
पुत्रास्त्रयोदश प्रोक्ता मनुना येन पूर्वशः ।
संतानकारणं तेषामौरसः पुत्रिका तथा ॥
transliteration: putrās trayodaśa proktā manunā yena pūrvaśaḥ | saṃtānakāraṇaṃ teṣām aurasaḥ putrikā tathā ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Thirteen types of sons are declared by Manu, the first among seers, for the purpose of lineage continuation; these include the legitimate son (aurasa) and the daughter's son (putrika), among others.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from the continuity of consciousness through santati (lineage)
Causation is established through dharmic role-bearing, not biological determinism alone
Capacity-based responsibility arises from acceptance of ancestral duty
Restoration logic ensures unbroken flow of dharma via designated heirs
Consciousness alignment occurs when roles in lineage are authentically assumed
executable_legal_axioms: IF a male heir is required to maintain santati THEN recognize up to thirteen categories of putra as defined by SPH-endorsed Smriti
IF legitimate son (aurasa) is present THEN prioritize him for all ancestral duties and rights
IF no aurasa THEN acknowledge putrika under same dharmic obligations
IF dispute arises in succession THEN resolution must align with consciousness recognition, not property accumulation
IF heir refuses dharmic duty THEN initiate nyaya process to restore capacity or reassign role
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, disputes concerning inheritance or lineage shall be resolved based on the ontological clarity of santati over material ownership. The court must ensure that the recognized heir—whether aurasa or putrika—is aligned with the continuation of dharma, not mere legal formalities.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa lies in the conscious acknowledgment of santati-dharma, not transactional proof of birth. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential responsibility within the lineage. Proportional responsibility flows from acceptance of role, not imposition of penalty. The non-punitive reality rule confirms that misalignment in succession requires completion, not condemnation.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate santati alignment dialogue between disputing parties
Assign spiritual mentor to guide reluctant heir into dharmic role
Facilitate ritual reintegration of estranged family members
Establish consciousness-based verification of intent to assume duty
Enforce role assumption through community witness, not coercive judgment
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law flows directly from His Avataric Intelligence. Dharma is restored through recognition of santati, not punishment. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator.
